title: Integral under a finite law
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a finite measure space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and let $s\subseteq\mathbb R$ be finite, with $X\in s$ almost everywhere. For every function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $\int f(X)\,d\mu=\sum_{x\in s}\mu(X=x)f(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $s$ is a finite subset of $\mathbb R$
replaced: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure, let $X:\Omega\to\bbr$ be measurable and supported almost everywhere on a finite set $s\subseteq\bbr$, and let $f:\bbr\to\bbr$ be arbitrary. Then $\int f(X)\,d\mu=\sum_{x\in s}\mu(X=x)f(x)$.
